source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Gather all the relevant inspection records, including the original fire-safety checklists, inspection notes, and any previous reports. Organize them chronologically to better understand the sequence of events.

3. Identify the failed items.
Conduct a thorough review of the inspection results to pinpoint which specific items failed to meet the fire-safety standards. This could include but is not limited to faulty fire alarms, sprinkler systems, emergency exits, fire doors, and the absence of clearly marked emergency exit signs.

4. Document deficiencies.
For each failed item, document in detail the nature of the deficiency. Include photos, diagrams, and descriptions outlining the issue(s). For example, a smoke detector may be absent altogether or simply malfunctioning.

5. Cite specific regulations.
Refer to the relevant local, state, and federal fire safety codes and regulations to cite the exact section(s) or rule(s) that the building has failed to meet. This legitimizes your document
